lines.trans: Good afternoon, Lemon Tree Inn in Valencia, Clara speaking—how may I help you today?
Who is calling at noon, Clara? Is another neighbour asking for a courtyard seat?
Yes, sir, read the station message slowly... arriving on the fast train at THREE?!
Three in the afternoon?! Wait—the anniversary tea is scheduled for six this evening!
Thank you very much for calling ahead—goodbye! Gentlemen, put down your teacups!
Did you just say our special guest arrives three full hours early?!
Track work moved his evening train onto the fast afternoon express into Valencia!
Three hours left! The cakes are still batter in the bowl, and the duet is half rehearsed!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Take one deep breath, boss, before you lose the glasses sitting on your nose.
First job: I sprint to the kitchen so Rocio heats both ovens right now!
Second job: Ernesto, send quick word down Calle de los Tilos inviting neighbours for half past three.
Wait—right after I checked in Rooms Two and Six, where did their keys go?!

words.gloss: to check in; to note down

words.gloss: to check in; to note down

lines.trans: See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: Standard farewell across the Spanish-speaking world.

examples.trans: Goodbye and have a good trip!
She said goodbye from the doorway.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Used for yearly celebrations of weddings, foundations, or historic dates.

examples.text: El próximo sábado celebramos el trigésimo aniversario en la posada.
examples.trans: Next Saturday we celebrate the thirtieth anniversary at the inn.

examples.text: Prepararon un pastel especial para el aniversario del barrio.
examples.trans: They baked a special cake for the neighbourhood anniversary.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.
Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Seat of a chair, bench, or train.

examples.text: El asiento de madera se dobla hacia arriba.
examples.trans: The wooden seat folds upward.

examples.text: Guardamos dos asientos junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: We saved two seats beside the window.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ayudar a + infinitive.

examples.trans: Shall I help you with those two boxes?

examples.text: Siempre ayudamos a los nuevos vecinos.
examples.trans: We always help the new neighbours.

meanings.note: Accented aún is interchangeable with todavía.

examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.

examples.text: Aún no han abierto la puerta.
examples.trans: They have not opened the door yet.

meanings.note: Plural adds -es (los boles); common in kitchens for mixing bowls and breakfast bowls.

examples.text: Dejamos reposar la masa de pan en un bol templado.
examples.trans: We let the bread dough rest in a warm bowl.

examples.text: Sirvió la sopa caliente en cuatro boles de cerámica.
examples.trans: She served the hot soup in four ceramic bowls.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

cambiar.gloss: to change; to swap; to exchange

meanings.en: to change; to swap; to exchange
meanings.note: Cambiar de habitación/camisa uses de before the noun.

examples.trans: I change the towels every morning.
We moved the table to a new spot.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday single-word opposite of rápido.

examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs.
Turn the wheel very slowly.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.
What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Plural los dúos.

examples.trans: The duet is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dúos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the duets from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Used for music, theatre, or practising a piece from start to finish.

examples.text: Carmen ensaya el vals en la galería silenciosa.
examples.trans: Carmen rehearses the waltz in the quiet sunroom.

examples.text: Ensayamos dos veces la pieza entera antes del viernes.
examples.trans: We rehearsed the whole piece twice before Friday.

meanings.note: Sigue entera = it is still in one piece.

examples.trans: It is a whole piece.
And your cup inside? Is it still in one piece?

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine; plural especiales.

examples.text: La tarta de limón es el postre especial de la casa.
examples.trans: Lemon tart is the house signature dessert.

examples.text: Viernes va a ser una noche muy especial aquí.
examples.trans: Friday is going to be a very special night here.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: La estación de tren = the train station.

examples.trans: The station is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stations from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?
He wears round glasses.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Hablo con mi familia cada domingo.
examples.trans: I speak with my family every Sunday.

examples.text: Hablamos largo rato bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We talked for a long while under the tree.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.
Keep looking toward the corner.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = take a deep breath.

examples.trans: It is a deep piece.

examples.text: Respire hondo, Ernesto. Todavía nadie ha escrito nada.
examples.trans: Take a deep breath, Ernesto. Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: ¿Qué hora es? asks the clock time.

examples.trans: The hour is here.

examples.text: Vemos las horas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hours from the door.

meanings.note: Del horno = out of the oven.

examples.trans: The oven is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hornos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ovens from the door.

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.
What are we having for breakfast today?

meanings.note: Plural los huéspedes.

examples.trans: The overnight guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huéspedes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the overnight guests from the door.

invitar.gloss: to invite; to treat (pick up the bill)

meanings.en: to invite; to treat (pick up the bill)
meanings.note: Invita la casa means 'it is on the house'.

examples.text: Hoy invito yo al café de la mañana.
examples.trans: Today morning coffee is my treat.

examples.text: Nos invitaron a cenar el sábado.
examples.trans: They invited us to dinner on Saturday.

meanings.note: Feminine: la jefa.

examples.trans: The boss is here.

examples.text: Vemos los jefes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bosss from the door.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: leyó, leyeron; past participle leído.

examples.text: Leo el periódico con el primer café.
examples.trans: I read the newspaper with my first coffee.

examples.text: Anoche leímos toda la carta juntos.
examples.trans: Last night we read the whole letter together.

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

llamar.gloss: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)

meanings.en: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)
meanings.note: ¿Cómo se llama? asks someone's name.

examples.trans: I am from here, pleased to meet you.
Someone called by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

examples.trans: I always arrive ten minutes early.

examples.text: El tren de Madrid llegó en punto.
examples.trans: The train from Madrid arrived on the dot.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Everyday synonym of enviar.

examples.text: Te mando un mensaje cuando llegue.
examples.trans: I will send you a message when I arrive.

examples.text: Mi primo me mandó naranjas de Valencia.
examples.trans: My cousin sent me oranges from Valencia.

meanings.note: Bread or pastry dough.

examples.text: La masa es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The dough is very important here.
We talk about the dough.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.
We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Mensaje de voz means 'voice message / voicemail'.

examples.text: Tienes un mensaje nuevo en el teléfono de recepción.
examples.trans: You have a new message on the front desk phone.

examples.text: Dejé un mensaje corto para confirmar la hora.
examples.trans: I left a short message to confirm the time.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meter.gloss: to put in; to tuck in

meanings.en: to put in; to tuck in
meanings.note: Everyday Spanish verb specifically for putting something inside a pocket, bag, or drawer.

examples.text: Meto las llaves en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: I put the keys in my pocket.

examples.text: Metimos las sillas dentro por la lluvia.
examples.trans: We brought the chairs inside because of the rain.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Plural las narices.

examples.trans: The nose is here.

examples.text: Vemos las narices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the noses from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

examples.text: Vamos a ver una obra de Henrik Ibsen.
examples.trans: We're going to see a play by Henrik Ibsen.
I obra

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: pido, pidió).

examples.text: Pido un café con leche, por favor.
examples.trans: I will order a coffee with milk, please.

examples.text: El cartero me pidió una firma.
examples.trans: The postman asked me for a signature.

perder.gloss: to lose; to leak (perder agua); to miss (a train)

meanings.en: to lose; to leak (perder agua); to miss (a train)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: pierde).

examples.text: Date prisa o perdemos el tren.
examples.trans: Hurry up or we will miss the train.

examples.text: La tubería vieja perdía unas gotas.
examples.trans: The old pipe was leaking a few drops.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.
The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose blue suitcase is this?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

examples.text: Te dejo a ti el recado.
examples.trans: I'll leave the message with you.
I have to run an errand.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = breathe deeply.

examples.text: Salgo al jardín a respirar aire fresco.
examples.trans: I step into the garden to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: Respiró hondo antes de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: He took a deep breath before ringing the bell.

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.trans: It is a fast piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

meanings.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather; a tiempo = on time.

examples.trans: The time is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tiempos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the times from the door.

meanings.note: Ir al trabajo = go to work.

examples.trans: The work is here.
